01

Procedural Task Training

Wheel Removal Training

One action leads to the next.

Interaction study / Sequence, tools & feedback

Position the jack

Align the jack with its highlighted target beneath the car, keeping the base grounded.

Slightly loosen every nut while the wheel is on the ground. The green highlight suggests the next nut in a star pattern.

Pump the jack handle to lift the vehicle. This step unlocks after all five nuts have been loosened.

Fully remove the nuts, pull off the wheel, and secure it in the designated rack to complete training.

A VR procedural training experience that teaches the sequence of removing a vehicle wheel through direct interaction with tools, guided actions, and immediate feedback.

The learning focus

Learning a sequence

Wall-mounted instructions and object highlights guide each action. Step gates keep the procedure in order; corrective messages explain what to do next while preserving valid progress.

A1 / Design documentRead the original ↗PDF · 2 pages · opens in a new tab
Guidance through interaction

Snap targets reduce placement precision, while the wrench still requires socket alignment. The next suggested lug nut glows green in a star pattern; the remaining nuts glow blue. After 18 seconds without progress, required highlights become brighter and pulse faster.

02

Spatial Navigation, Teleportation and Scene Switching

Garage Ready

Two spaces. One preparation loop.

Interaction study / Linked scenes & persistent inventory

Find what's missing

Home Garage

Start at the Home Garage task board. Tire care, wiper care, and oil service preparation each call for different supplies and reusable tools.

Auto Parts Store

Travel to the Auto Parts Store. Use six signed departments, the directory, and the left-hand map and checklist to locate the missing supplies.

Home Garage

Return to the Home Garage. Store new purchases, retrieve saved tools, and bring reusable tools to the workbench before confirming readiness.

A VR learning experience where users navigate between a home garage and an auto parts store, locate supplies, organize equipment, and reuse tools across multiple preparation tasks.

The learning focus

Learning across spaces

Three tasks cover tire care, wiper care, and oil service preparation. Inventory and storage locations persist between scenes during the session, so earlier purchases can become tools for later tasks.

A2 / Design documentRead the original ↗PDF · 1 page · opens in a new tab
Movement and wayfinding

Teleportation, continuous movement, and 45-degree snap turning are available together. Overhead signs, a store directory, north-up maps, and a left-hand checklist support wayfinding. Labeled exit doors switch scenes with a fade and a short arrival sound. Headset comfort still needs evaluation.

03 / An ongoing exploration

A sequence to follow. A space to remember. Tools to put into practice.

These projects explore different parts of skill learning: procedural guidance, spatial familiarity, and hands-on preparation. The collection will grow as new assignments explore other skills and interaction systems. Learning benefits remain design goals, rather than measured outcomes.
